minutes.headline: Parks Commission heard the Marshall Park schematic design, made no formal votes on it, and approved minutes.
minutes.summary: The meeting was mostly the design team's schematic design presentation for Marshall Park, followed by commissioner and wetlands-expert feedback. The commission also heard a recreation and Town Beach update (sand permit, swim lessons), reviewed a draft naming and sponsorship policy that was held for public feedback, and approved two sets of minutes after amending one. The next meeting was set for July 12.

budget_items.topic: Solitude contract for Town Beach weed/sand work
budget_items.what_was_said: The contract so far covers only the permit; the remainder can be released after the fiscal year turns because it is an FY24 capital project.
The chair worried about leaving money unspent on Park accounts; the facilities director said money was moved into accounts to spend it all without overages, with accounting staff retiring.

budget_items.topic: Town Beach seasonal memberships and swim lessons
budget_items.what_was_said: Seasonal memberships are scanned into the registration system; swim lesson sessions are largely full.
Discussion of the volume of sand requested from Conservation; the facilities director said this request was smaller than a prior one.

budget_items.topic: Green Communities state funding for Marshall Park
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair proposed reaching out to the Green Communities committee about state money for items such as LED lights; Pat agreed to send an email.
figures_as_heard: up to 100 of anything up to I think 150 000

budget_items.topic: Grant application for the park program
budget_items.what_was_said: A basis of design report is being prepared for accessibility and sustainability language; the grant is due in mid-July and the commission will review it at a July 12 meeting.
Draft policy lets businesses and others contribute financially in exchange for naming rights; details to be worked out case by case.

decisions.decision: Design team will look at adding a gate at the Chestnut Street emergency access; chair suggested placing it at the walk path rather than at the street.
Chair preferred keeping the main path fully universal for now and not adding a stair connection to the Little League field; no objection recorded.
Chair asked that the historic stones of the entrance wall be noted for salvage; design team did not object.
Commissioners agreed to attend the Conservation Commission meeting (expected July 5) to support the Town Beach sand request.
Pat agreed to contact the Green Communities committee about funding for Marshall Park.
Naming and sponsorship policy will not be voted on yet; it will be posted as a draft for community feedback and tabled until a full commission is present.
Next meeting set for July 12 to review the grant application.
Minutes language amended to say previous discussions were that a plan to establish a new t-ball location comes before removing t-ball at Marshall.
Boys and Girls Club polar plunge idea to be put on a future agenda, possibly July 12.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission heard the design team's schematic design presentation for Marshall Park and took no formal vote on it.
Commissioners and a wetlands expert gave feedback; the design team will look at a gate at the Chestnut Street emergency access.
The draft naming and sponsorship policy will not be voted on yet; it will be posted for community feedback and tabled until a full commission is present.
Commissioners agreed to support the Town Beach sand request at the Conservation Commission, and Pat agreed to contact the Green Communities committee about funding for Marshall Park.
Minutes were approved after the t-ball wording was amended; the outcome of the vote was not audible. The next meeting was set for July 12.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park is still at schematic design, so layout choices such as the entrance gate, path access and salvage of the historic entrance stones can still change before a grant application and any funding request.
A policy letting businesses and others pay for naming rights could change who funds town parks, and residents can comment on the draft before the commission votes.
watch_next: July 12 commission meeting to review the Marshall Park grant application, due in mid-July.
Conservation Commission meeting, expected July 5, on the Town Beach sand request.
